questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In a series $RLC$ AC circuit driven at angular frequency $\omega$, the resistance is $R = 30\ \Omega$, inductive reactance is $X_L = 70\ \Omega$, and capacitive reactance is $X_C = 30\ \Omega$. The power factor $\cos\phi$ of the circuit is
questions.explanationEn: The impedance is $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = \sqrt{30^2 + 40^2} = 50\ \Omega$. Thus the power factor is $\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{30}{50} = 0.60$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A plane electromagnetic wave of average intensity $I$ is incident normally on a flat surface. The ratio of the radiation pressure exerted on a perfectly reflecting mirror to that exerted on a perfectly absorbing black surface is
questions.explanationEn: For normal incidence, $P_{\text{abs}} = \frac{I}{c}$ and $P_{\text{ref}} = \frac{2I}{c}$ (momentum reverses upon reflection), so their ratio is $2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A planar current loop of area $A$ carrying steady current $I$ has magnetic dipole moment $\vec{m} = m\hat{n}$. When placed in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ at angle $\theta$ between $\vec{m}$ and $\vec{B}$, the net force and the magnitude of the torque on the loop are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: In a uniform magnetic field, the net force on any closed current loop is $\vec{F} = I(\oint d\vec{l})\times\vec{B} = \vec{0}$, while the torque is $\vec{\tau} = \vec{m}\times\vec{B}$ with magnitude $IAB\sin\theta$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A non-relativistic proton enters a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ perpendicularly with speed $v$ and executes circular motion with time period $T$. If a second proton enters the same magnetic field perpendicularly with speed $2v$, its time period is
questions.explanationEn: The cyclotron period $T = \frac{2\pi m}{qB}$ is independent of the particle's speed $v$ (non-relativistically), so the period remains $T$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A beam of singly charged ions enters a region containing crossed uniform electric field $\vec{E} = E_0\hat{y}$ and magnetic field $\vec{B} = B_0\hat{z}$. For an ion moving along $+\hat{x}$ to pass through undeflected, its speed must be
questions.explanationEn: The Lorentz force is $\vec{F} = q(E_0\hat{y} + v\hat{x}\times B_0\hat{z}) = q(E_0 - vB_0)\hat{y}$. Setting $\vec{F} = \vec{0}$ gives $v = \frac{E_0}{B_0}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A parallel-plate capacitor of plate area $A$ and plate separation $d$ has air capacitance $C_0$. A dielectric slab of area $A$, thickness $d/2$, and relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r = 3$ is inserted parallel to the plates. The new capacitance is
questions.explanationEn: The capacitor behaves as two capacitors in series: an air gap of thickness $d/2$ ($C_1 = 2C_0$) and a dielectric layer of thickness $d/2$ ($C_2 = 2\varepsilon_r C_0 = 6C_0$). Thus $C = \frac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} = \frac{12C_0}{8} = \frac{3}{2}C_0$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For a sinusoidal plane electromagnetic wave propagating in a lossless linear medium of permittivity $\varepsilon$ and permeability $\mu$, the ratio of the time-averaged electric energy density $\langle u_E \rangle$ to the time-averaged magnetic energy density $\langle u_B \rangle$ is
questions.explanationEn: Since $E_0 = v B_0 = \frac{B_0}{\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}}$, we have $\langle u_E \rangle = \frac{1}{4}\varepsilon E_0^2 = \frac{1}{4}\varepsilon\left(\frac{B_0^2}{\mu\varepsilon}\right) = \frac{B_0^2}{4\mu} = \langle u_B \rangle$. Thus the ratio is $1$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A plane electromagnetic wave of average intensity $I$ is incident on a perfectly reflecting flat mirror at an angle of incidence $\theta$ with respect to the surface normal. The radiation pressure exerted on the mirror is
questions.explanationEn: The power intercepted per unit surface area is $I\cos\theta$, and the normal component of momentum change per unit energy upon perfect reflection is $\frac{2\cos\theta}{c}$. Multiplying gives $P_{\text{rad}} = \frac{2I\cos^2\theta}{c}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total electrostatic self-energy required to assemble a uniformly charged solid non-conducting sphere of total charge $Q$ and radius $R$ in vacuum is
questions.explanationEn: Integrating $U = \int \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2\,d\tau$ gives $U_{\text{in}} = \frac{Q^2}{40\pi\varepsilon_0 R}$ and $U_{\text{out}} = \frac{Q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0 R}$. Summing both yields $U = \left(\frac{1}{40} + \frac{5}{40}\right)\frac{Q^2}{\pi\varepsilon_0 R} = \frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0 R}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Twelve identical resistors, each of resistance $R$, are connected along the twelve edges of a cube. The equivalent resistance measured between two diagonally opposite corners (across a body diagonal) of the cube is
questions.explanationEn: By symmetry, a current $I$ entering one corner splits equally into three edges ($I/3$ each), then splits into six edges ($I/6$ each), and finally recombines through three edges ($I/3$ each) into the opposite corner. The total voltage drop is $V = \left(\frac{I}{3} + \frac{I}{6} + \frac{I}{3}\right)R = \frac{5}{6}IR$, so $R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{5}{6}R$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a static charge-free region of space where the electrostatic potential $V(x, y, z)$ satisfies Laplace's equation $\nabla^2 V = 0$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: The value of $V$ at any interior point equals the average of $V$ over any spherical surface centered at that point lying wholly within the region
$V$ cannot have a strict local maximum or strict local minimum anywhere in the interior of the charge-free region
The electric field magnitude $|\vec{E}|$ must be spatially constant throughout the region
A free point test charge cannot be held in stable mechanical equilibrium solely by electrostatic forces in this region
questions.explanationEn: Harmonic functions ($\nabla^2 V = 0$) obey the mean-value theorem and have no interior local extrema (first two True), which directly implies Earnshaw's theorem: no stable electrostatic equilibrium for a point charge (True). However, $|\vec{E}|$ need not be uniform—for instance $V = x^2 - y^2$ has $\nabla^2 V = 0$ and non-uniform $\vec{E}$ (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A series $RLC$ circuit is driven by a sinusoidal AC source of constant RMS voltage $V_0$ and variable angular frequency $\omega$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: At resonance, the instantaneous voltage across the inductor and the instantaneous voltage across the capacitor are in phase with each other
At the resonant frequency $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$, the circuit impedance reaches its minimum value $Z = R$
The half-power bandwidth of the resonance curve is $\Delta\omega = \frac{R}{L}$
For $\omega > \omega_0$, the circuit is net inductive and the current lags the source voltage
questions.explanationEn: At $\omega = \omega_0$, $X_L = X_C$ so $Z_{\min} = R$ (True). For $\omega > \omega_0$, $X_L > X_C$ so current lags voltage (True). Bandwidth is $\Delta\omega = \omega_0 / Q = R/L$ (True). At resonance, $V_L$ and $V_C$ have equal amplitudes and are $180^\circ$ out of phase (canceling each other), not in phase (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Compare a plane monochromatic electromagnetic wave propagating in a good conductor ($\sigma \gg \omega\varepsilon$) versus a lossless non-magnetic dielectric ($\sigma = 0, \varepsilon_r > 1$). Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: In a good conductor, the magnetic energy density greatly exceeds the electric energy density
In a good conductor, the skin depth increases as the electrical conductivity $\sigma$ increases
In a lossless dielectric, the wave amplitude remains constant as it propagates and $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ are in phase
In a good conductor, the magnetic field lags behind the electric field by a phase angle of approximately $45^\circ$
questions.explanationEn: In a good conductor, the complex wavevector $k = (1 + i)/\delta$ gives $\vec{B} = (k/\omega)(\hat{n}\times\vec{E})$, so $\vec{B}$ lags $\vec{E}$ by $45^\circ$ (True) and $u_B / u_E \approx \sigma/(\omega\varepsilon) \gg 1$ (True). In a lossless dielectric, $k$ is real so there is no attenuation and $\vec{E}, \vec{B}$ are in phase (True). Since $\delta = \sqrt{2/(\mu\sigma\omega)}$, higher $\sigma$ decreases $\delta$ (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about magnetic forces on steady current-carrying conductors is/are correct?
optionsEn: A semicircular wire of radius $R$ carrying current $I$ in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ perpendicular to its plane experiences the same net magnetic force as a straight wire of length $2R$ carrying current $I$ along its diameter
Two long perpendicular (skew) wires carrying steady currents exert zero net torque on each other
Two long parallel wires carrying steady currents in the same direction attract each other
The net magnetic force on any closed rigid current loop placed in a spatially uniform magnetic field is zero
questions.explanationEn: Parallel currents attract (True), a closed loop in uniform $\vec{B}$ has $\vec{F} = I(\oint d\vec{l})\times\vec{B} = \vec{0}$ (True), and for any open wire in uniform $\vec{B}$, $\vec{F} = I\vec{L}_{\text{eff}}\times\vec{B}$ depends only on the vector displacement between endpoints ($2R$, True). Skew perpendicular wires exert a non-zero torque tending to align them parallel (False).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A $24\text{ V}$ ideal DC voltage source is connected across a series combination of a $4\ \Omega$ resistor and an $8\ \Omega$ resistor. The Thevenin equivalent voltage across the terminals of the $8\ \Omega$ resistor is ______ $\text{V}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By voltage division, the open-circuit voltage across the $8\ \Omega$ resistor is $V_{\text{th}} = 24 \times \frac{8}{4 + 8} = 16\text{ V}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: An AC voltage source of $100\text{ V}$ (RMS) drives a series $RC$ circuit with resistance $R = 60\ \Omega$ and capacitive reactance $X_C = 80\ \Omega$. The RMS current in the circuit is ______ $\text{A}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The impedance is $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2} = \sqrt{60^2 + 80^2} = 100\ \Omega$, so $I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{Z} = \frac{100}{100} = 1\text{ A}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Three point charges $+q$, $+q$, and $-2q$ are placed at the three vertices of an equilateral triangle of side $a$. If the total electrostatic potential energy of the system is $\frac{\alpha q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 a}$, the integer value of $\alpha$ is ______. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Summing over all three pairs: $U = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 a}[(+q)(+q) + (+q)(-2q) + (+q)(-2q)] = \frac{-3q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 a}$, so $\alpha = -3$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A $100$-turn flat coil of area $0.02\text{ m}^2$ is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field that decreases linearly from $0.5\text{ T}$ to $0.1\text{ T}$ in $0.04\text{ s}$. The magnitude of the induced emf in the coil is ______ $\text{V}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By Faraday's law, $|\mathcal{E}| = N A \left|\frac{\Delta B}{\Delta t}\right| = 100 \times 0.02 \times \frac{0.4}{0.04} = 20\text{ V}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A series $RLC$ circuit contains an inductor $L = 100\text{ mH}$, a capacitor $C = 10\ \mu\text{F}$, and a resistor $R = 20\ \Omega$. Its resonant angular frequency $\omega_0$ is ______ $\text{rad/s}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The resonant angular frequency is $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{0.1 \times 10^{-5}}} = \frac{1}{10^{-3}} = 1000\text{ rad/s}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Electricity and Magnetism (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A long cylindrical capacitor has inner conductor radius $a = 1.0\text{ cm}$ and outer conductor radius $b = 4.0\text{ cm}$. The space between the conductors is completely filled with a dielectric of relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r = 2.0$. Taking $\varepsilon_0 = 8.854 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F/m}$, the capacitance per unit length is ______ $\text{pF/m}$. (Round off to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: For a dielectric-filled cylindrical capacitor, $\frac{C}{L} = \frac{2\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r}{\ln(b/a)} = \frac{2\pi(8.854 \times 10^{-12})(2.0)}{\ln 4} \approx 80.26 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F/m} = 80.26\text{ pF/m}$.
